questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Academic relevance (Milan for MA in History of Art) and availability of English language courses.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Easy and accessible, I did not have any problems in this regard.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had to show up at the international student desk - there was nothing particularly complicated that I needed help with.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Difficult - Milan is a tricky city to find reliable and affordable accomodation in. I ended up finding a room through
Spacest.com
and had a good experience renting a room from an Italian woman who also made sure to check in with me and make sure that I was okay, but I had little guarantee before leaving that it was going to work out.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Living off campus can really help you connect more with the local environment and community, getting to know ordinary coffee shops etc. instead of just meeting other students. It can be difficult to check whether the housing that you have found is trustworthy before getting there, but it is important to try. I know some others that found something together with people from their sending institution, which seemed like a good idea - they knew they had someone to rely on if anything happened.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: One course had a completely different proces of registration than all the other courses, which was not very clear on the programme website - I ultimately had to take a different course because of this, as it had filled up by the time I found out.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Online registration through the university website, I had to add the name of the course, the professor, and the amount of ECTS credits on a list, which could later be updated easily.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I never needed it, but I assume that I could have contacted the international student desk.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Mostly succesfull, but not fully - I had problems registering for one out of four classes. This was due to very limited spots in the class as well as a lack of transparency regarding the process of signing up for this one particular type of class on the programme website.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Avoid trying to sign up for any workshop-classes, as they have a different process of signing up and some only have 8 spots available. Spend some extra time trying to figure out which other classes in English are available. Some courses are available for different amounts of ECTS credits, so you might be able to mix and match a bit to make sure you have the required amount for Erasmus but not too many for your home university.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was really satisfied with half my courses, where the professors were engaging and the topics clear, relevant, and maintained a high academic standard. The other half I found the teaching methods somewhat outdated and the topic of the classes and the exams unclear - I think it depends a lot on the individual professor.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I found that half of my courses were very relevant and maintained a high standard, while the other half seemed less relevant and the teaching goals of those courses were a bit unclear.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I found that they were more focused on memorization than discussion (or analysis for that matter), which I did not expect from MA classes. The teaching style was very different, with little in-class engagement with the students, although this depended a lot on the individual professor.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Ancient Documents in Their Visual and Performative Context
Computational Methods and Techniques for Historical and Cultural Studies 
Cultural History of the Modern Period
The Politics of Mobility, Displacement and Asylum

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: "Ancient Documents in Their Visual and Performative Context" and "The Politics of Mobility, Displacement and Asylum" I would absolutely recommend! Professor Lucia Cecchet ("Ancient documents...") and professor Luca Ciabarri ("The Politics...") were engaging, the structure of the courses was clear, and they maintained a high academic level in a welcoming learning environment.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: It was sometimes difficult to find space in the libraries, so I ended up sitting more in cafés than I do at home.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I think the high rent in the city meant that I expected other neccessities to be very expensive as well, which (by my home country's standards) they are not - although it is definitely more expensive than most other Italian cities.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were discounts for some cultural institutions - other than that I mostly encountered ESN Milano. The events ESN Milano organized seemed interesting, but sadly they usually filled up very quickly, and I only managed to go to their weekly meeting at a bar.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I recommend going to some of the meet-ups early on - I met some of my closest friends there. Don't be afraid to ask your classmates to get coffee after class!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on day-trips to near-by cities, I especially recommend Bergamo and Lecco. A lot of the museums have really good student discounts. Some of the art museums that I enjoyed the most were Novecento, Pinacoteca di Brera, Pinacoteca Ambrosiana, GAM, and Fondazione Prada.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I was fairly easy - Milan is also a very international city, so it might have made it easier. I think most of my friends found the city and culture welcoming, even if we came from completely different parts of the world.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go for a coffee or try to organize aperitivo with the people in your classes - this is easier if you mostly follow courses from one degree.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I think the cultural differences were mostly interesting, not particularly challenging. I think I was also fortunate to be surrounded by kind and open-minded people.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really appreciated how open and easy to talk to my fellow students were - and I really enjoyed how easy it was to grab a quick coffee or a quick drink. It didn't have to be a big, planned thing, which I really enjoyed. I also really liked going to the different markets and seeing the city that way.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Put yourself in situations without a lot of other UCPH students - there's a lot of us, but I think a big part of the experience is getting out of a Danish bubble. 
Don't expect the teaching styles to be similar to the ones in UCPH: it's a very different approach, but even if it's not to your preference, it teaches you something about how academia works. 
You can follow courses as an attending or non-attending student, but I would definitely recommend being an attending student, as it provides both structure and is a great way of meeting friends and experiencing academic culture.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Some of the courses are available for different amounts of ECTS credits, so you might be able to take a 9 ECTS course as a 6 ECTS course, which can make it easier to get the correct amount of ECTS credits.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people I met! Spending time experiencing the city with new friends and just taking time to do so. Milan is really beautiful and full of culture and things to see, whether it's markets, museums, restaurants or architecture.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I think adjusting to some of the different teaching approaches, but also the exam season was quite intense (three exams in one week). I definitely spend more time studying for each exam than I needed to, as the grading system seemed more relaxed than it is in UCPH (in my experience, at least).

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
